text:
alert-bot: HIGH: eu-central GPU pool saturation detected. Autoscaler hit configured maxNodes=32. PodPending count: 95. Trigger: queue_length > 1500 for 10m. Pager to #incidents and paging rota.

sam (sre/oncall): I'm oncall. Pulling logs and cluster view. Current queue ~1600, 95 Pending pods, 410 Running. Kube-scheduler: insufficient GPUs reported.

maria (infra): nodepool: gpu-inference-euc, min=8 max=32. Cloud quota for GPUs shows 32. No recent deploys that should spike usage AFAICT.

dev-ops: telemetry shows 4x increase in short-running streaming requests from a single tenant over last 20m. Might be a customer load test or runaway job.

sam (sre/oncall): tagging customer-facing CS. @cs-rep can you confirm if they rolled out a change? Also listing high-impact routes in console.

cs-rep: pinged account manager; customer says they started a stress test but thought it was in staging. Flagging high priority. They may roll back.

sre-manager: immediate mitigations: 1) isolate offending tenant by rate-limiting or routing to degraded tier. 2) request emergency quota bump while we prepare node reclamation. 3) consider evicting best-effort workloads.

maria (infra): preparing manual quota request to cloud for +16 GPUs temporary. Need sign-off from finance for accelerated quota. Meanwhile I can mark non-prod nodepools for drain.

sam (sre/oncall): configuring rate-limit rule to cap tenant throughput to 50 rps, applying now.

sam (sre/oncall): command run:
```
redwoodctl routing create rate-limit --tenant tenant-42 --limit 50 --window 60s
```

sam (sre/oncall): rule applied. Observed immediate drop in incoming queue slope. Pending pods still building.

dev-ops: discovered several legacy jobs targeting gpu labels from experiments namespace. Recommend preemptively scaling those down.

maria (infra): running targeted cordon/drain of 4 non-prod nodes (freeing 16 GPUs). Commands:
```
kubectl cordon node-exp-{01..04}
kubectl drain node-exp-{01..04} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
```

maria (infra): drain finished, freed GPUs. Scheduler placed ~40 pods onto freed capacity. Queue down to ~900.

sam (sre/oncall): still seeing some image-pull backoffs on a few worker images. Registry rate-limits might delay reschedules. Switching to pre-pulled warm node image for critical workers.

dev-ops: deploying image-pull-job to prefetch images on ready nodes. Should help speed scheduling.

sre-manager: status update: requested quota increase (+16 GPUs) submitted to cloud via console as expedited. Infra will follow up with finance approval.

maria (infra): cloud responded: request received, need billing confirmation. infra-manager looped in finance lead.

sam (sre/oncall): to reduce pressure on node provisioner, I'm temporarily enabling model-oversub setting to allow 2 smaller models per GPU for low-priority routes. Applying now.

sam (sre/oncall): patch applied: runtime-config MODEL_OVERSUB_LOWPRIO=2. Watching for correctness.

cs-rep: customer update posted: "We're aware of degraded performance in eu-central while we mitigate high load. We've applied temporary rate limits and are working on capacity. Will follow up." Customers acknowledged.

maria (infra): quota approved by cloud and applied. nodepool maxNodes updated 32 -> 48. Autoscaler kicked off; provisioning 16 new nodes.

dev-ops: note: provisioning slow because instance type blush with startup scripts; will monitor.

sam (sre/oncall): new nodes joining. Once Ready, scheduler drains queue faster. Current queue ~260. 5xx spike returning to baseline.

sre-manager: actions summary: 1) tenant rate-limited, 2) non-prod drained to free 16 GPUs, 3) quota raised +16 and nodes provisioned, 4) model oversub for low-priority, 5) prefetch images to reduce pull delays.

sam (sre/oncall): I'm going to keep monitoring for 45m. Handoff to sre-manager for post-incident follow-up: create incident ticket and schedule postmortem to review autoscaler maxNodes policy, tenant isolation controls, and registry pull throttles.

sre-manager: taking over. Incident -> MONITORING. Filing ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2801234567. CS to send customer follow-up and offer credits if SLA breach confirmed.

sam (sre/oncall): thanks team. :thumbsup: 

end of thread.
